title: Caesar Dressing
subtitle: Classic Caesar salad dressing with anchovies and Parmesan
excerpt: The deeply savoury, creamy dressing that defines the Caesar salad: anchovies, garlic, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, and Parmesan, whisked into a glossy, coating emulsion.

recipe.sourceNotes: Caesar dressing takes its name from Caesar Cardini, an Italian-born restaurateur who operated restaurants on both sides of the US-Mexico border. The dressing was first created at his restaurant in Tijuana, Mexico, around 1924. The original contained Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, egg, and Parmesan; anchovies were added to later versions (possibly by Caesar's brother Alex). The original dressing was made tableside with whole leaves of romaine lettuce, which were picked up and eaten with the fingers. Today the dressing is usually emulsified with the egg yolk (or mayonnaise for a quicker version), which gives it the thick, creamy, coating consistency associated with Caesar salad in restaurants worldwide.

content.text: Mash the anchovy fillets to a paste before whisking them into the dressing: this distributes the flavour evenly without chunks. The Parmesan is stirred in at the end rather than emulsified with the oil; it adds body and salt. The dressing should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. For a safer alternative to the raw egg yolk, substitute 2 tablespoons of good-quality mayonnaise and skip the egg.

items.preparation: in oil; mashed to a paste
minced to a paste with a pinch of salt

content.text: Put the anchovy paste, garlic paste, egg yolk, Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Whisk until smooth and combined.

Slowly drizzle in the olive oil while whisking constantly until the dressing is thick, creamy, and emulsified. Stir in the grated Parmesan. Taste: it should be deeply savoury, sharp, and well-seasoned.
Use straight away to dress a Caesar salad. To store, pour into a sealed jar and refrigerate for up to 3 days. It thickens when cold; stir in a little cold water to loosen it before use.
